items.name: Trust Blue
items.mood: Calm institutional confidence — the blue a buyer expects when they are about to put a credit card on file for their whole team.

items.name: Ledger Emerald
items.mood: Money that is being counted carefully — deep green over graphite, serious rather than startup-cheerful; reach for it when the product moves real balances.

items.name: Chain Gold
items.mood: Bullion on carbon — gold against near-black with an electric violet spark; for crypto and trading products that want weight instead of neon toy energy.

items.name: Clinical Teal
items.mood: Clean, unhurried and non-alarming — teal and cool white that reads as competent care rather than emergency; for anything a patient reads while anxious.

items.name: Shopfront Orange
items.mood: Warm retail urgency — burnt orange that makes a Buy button feel inviting instead of shouty, with a green accent reserved for 'in stock' and confirmation.

items.name: Atelier Noir
items.mood: Editorial luxury — near-black, bone white and a single champagne gold, with nothing else competing; for fashion houses and anything sold on restraint.

items.name: Trattoria Tomato
items.mood: Appetite on a cream tablecloth — tomato red with olive and warm paper; for menus, ordering and anything that should make you hungry rather than efficient.

items.name: Spa Blush
items.mood: Exhaling — dusty rose and sage on warm plaster, quiet and skin-adjacent; for beauty, spa and wellness where a hard edge would break the spell.

items.name: Volt Athletic
items.mood: The last rep — volt green screaming off charcoal, high-energy and legible mid-workout at arm's length; for training apps and performance gear.

items.name: Campus Indigo
items.mood: Approachable scholarship — indigo with a highlighter amber, friendly enough for a teenager and credible enough for the institution paying for it.

items.name: Playroom Pop
items.mood: Primary-colour joy with the volume up — bright blue, sunshine yellow and a candy red, sized for small fingers and short attention spans.

items.name: Arcade Neon
items.mood: A dark room lit by a screen — magenta and cyan burning on true black; for games, launchers and anything that should feel like it hums.

items.name: Primetime Red
items.mood: Lights down, poster art up — signature red on cinema black where every pixel of chrome gets out of the artwork's way; for streaming and video.

items.name: Amp Purple
items.mood: Stage-light purple with a hot pink spill — nocturnal and loud; for music players, artist pages and release drops.

items.name: Broadsheet Ink
items.mood: Newsprint authority — black on paper with one red for the thing that matters; for journalism, longform and anything where the words are the design.

items.name: Studio Canvas
items.mood: Gallery walls — warm paper, ink and a burnt-orange hyperlink; deliberately quiet so the work in the grid is the only loud thing.

items.name: Agency Acid
items.mood: Confident and slightly rude — near-black with an acid lime that behaves like a highlighter; for agencies selling taste and nerve.

items.name: Devtool Slate
items.mood: Built for people who live in a terminal but ship a GUI — slate chrome that gets out of the way, and an emerald that only ever means 'passing'.

items.name: Neural Iris
items.mood: Iris violet bleeding into cyan — the current house style for anything with a model behind it; use it when the product should feel generative, not corporate.

items.name: Signal Cyan
items.mood: A wall of numbers that stays readable at 2am — deep blue-slate with cyan and amber reserved strictly for series colour and thresholds.

items.name: Focus Graphite
items.mood: A desk with nothing on it — warm graphite and paper with a single amber for the one thing due today; for writing, notes and task tools.

items.name: Feed Fuchsia
items.mood: Warm, social and a little hot — fuchsia with a tangerine like a sunset gradient pulled apart into two usable tokens; for feeds and profiles.

items.name: Voyage Sky
items.mood: Window seat at altitude — clean sky blue over sand with a coral for fares and deals; optimistic without tipping into travel-brochure cliché.

items.name: Estate Sage
items.mood: Old money without the crest — sage green, limestone and brass; for property listings that should feel like a considered purchase, not a lead form.

items.name: Torque Steel
items.mood: Machined gunmetal with a brake-light red — engineered, masculine-leaning and cold to the touch; for cars, hardware and configurators.

items.name: Chambers Oxblood
items.mood: Leather-bound and unbothered — oxblood on cream with brass; for law firms and advisory work where blue would read as a tech startup.

items.name: Kindred Green
items.mood: Hopeful and human — a living green with a coral for urgency; for charities that need to ask for money without feeling like a bank or a guilt trip.

items.name: Civic Navy
items.mood: Plain-spoken public service — federal navy, generous neutrals and no decoration; built to survive a screen reader, a 5-year-old laptop and a lawsuit.

items.name: Freight Amber
items.mood: Hi-vis on steel — warehouse amber against industrial grey with a green that only ever means delivered; for logistics, fleet and ops screens.

items.name: People Plum
items.mood: Warm plum and a teal that keeps it professional — softer than corporate blue, which matters when the screen is about someone's salary or leave.

items.name: Bazaar Teal
items.mood: Two-sided and busy in a good way — deep teal for the platform, tangerine for the transaction; keeps buyer and seller surfaces distinguishable.

items.name: Heartline Rose
items.mood: Flushed but not tacky — rose and peach with a violet undertow; for dating and relationship products that want warmth without a heart-shaped cursor.

items.name: Stadium Scarlet
items.mood: Kickoff — scarlet on midnight with a floodlight yellow; built for live scores, big numbers and being read from the back of the room.

items.name: Darkroom Amber
items.mood: Safelight — neutral greys calibrated to not lie about a photograph, with amber as the only chroma in the chrome; for galleries and photo tools.

items.name: Minimal Mono
items.mood: Nothing but greys and one blue that only appears when you can click it — the safest possible starting point when the content has to carry the design.

items.name: Brutalist Concrete
items.mood: Unfinished on purpose — raw concrete, hard black rules and a warning yellow; for portfolios and brands that want to look like they don't care.

items.name: Terminal Phosphor
items.mood: A CRT that never got switched off — phosphor green on near-black with amber for warnings; for CLIs, logs and anything that should feel close to the metal.

items.name: Pastel Soft
items.mood: Sherbet surfaces with grown-up text — lilac, mint and peach kept as backgrounds while every foreground stays dark enough to actually read.

items.name: Earthy Organic
items.mood: Clay, moss and oat — pigments that look mixed rather than picked; for sustainable brands, ceramics and food that wants to smell like soil.

items.name: High Contrast Accessible
items.mood: Every pair pushed well past AA and most of the way to AAA — the palette to reach for when low vision, sunlight or a legal accessibility floor is the constraint.
